sections.title: Growth and features
sections.text: Sesamum alatum is an erect annual herb, usually 20–90 cm tall and occasionally reaching 1.5 m. Lower leaves are divided into three to five narrow lobes; upper leaves are simple and narrow. Its pink or purple flowers are about 2–3 cm long, and the narrow capsule bears small seeds with conspicuous wings.

sections.title: Food use
sections.text: Sesamum alatum is a different species from cultivated sesame, S. indicum. PROTA reports that its leaves and young shoots are eaten cooked, and that the seeds are sometimes eaten or pressed for oil. The African Pharmacopoeia also recognizes its seeds as sesame seed.

sections.title: Plate check
sections.text: The paired plate shows broad, toothed leaves, whereas the described species has lower leaves divided into narrow lobes and entire-edged upper leaves. The mismatched plate is therefore not displayed.
